title: Notices and records after substituting an interchangeable biological product
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 12EE(d), within a reasonable time following any substitution of an interchangeable biological product, the dispensing pharmacist or the pharmacist's designee shall notify the prescribing practitioner of the substitution, and the notification shall be conveyed by a notation in the patient's interoperable electronic health record; if the pharmacist does not have the ability to make such a notation, the notification shall be conveyed by facsimile, electronic transmission or by making a notation in the patient's record maintained by the pharmacy which is accessible to the practitioner by request; and a pharmacist who utilizes an interoperable electronic prescribing technology shall enter the substitution into the patient's electronic health record. Under § 12EE(e), following any such substitution, the dispensing pharmacist or the pharmacist's designee shall notify the patient, or the patient's authorized representative, of the substitution; the notification shall be written and may be conveyed by facsimile, electronic transmission, a notation in the patient's record system shared with the prescriber or another means consistent with prevailing pharmacy practice in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D. Under § 12EE(f) the dispensing pharmacist or the pharmacist's designee, the prescribing provider and the administering practitioner shall retain a record of each substitution of an interchangeable biological product dispensed for not less than 1 year from the date of the last entry in the profile record, and nothing in that subsection limits the application of the professional standards for registered pharmacists, pharmacies and pharmacy departments promulgated by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy. Under § 12EE(g), in the event of noncompliance by a pharmacist or a practitioner, the purchaser or patient may inform the director of consumer affairs and business regulation of the noncompliance, as provided in M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D.
exam_relevance: Tests who receives which notice after a biological substitution, the reasonable-time clock for the prescriber notice and the written form of the patient notice, the fallback methods for reaching the prescriber, and the retention of not less than one year measured from the last entry in the profile record by three record holders.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws, substitution of interchangeable biological product by pharmacist

numeric_facts.fact: Retention of the record of each substitution of an interchangeable biological product
numeric_facts.conditions: Not less than 1 year from the date of the last entry in the profile record; retained by the dispensing pharmacist or designee, the prescribing provider and the administering practitioner

exceptions: Where the pharmacist does not have the ability to make a notation in the patient's interoperable electronic health record, the prescriber notice is conveyed by facsimile, electronic transmission or a notation in the patient's record maintained by the pharmacy that is accessible to the practitioner by request.
common_confusions: Treating the prescriber notice as something to complete before substituting. M.G.L. c. 112, § 12EE(d) runs within a reasonable time following the substitution.
Giving the patient an oral notice only. M.G.L. c. 112, § 12EE(e) requires the patient notification to be written.
Measuring the one-year retention from the dispensing date. M.G.L. c. 112, § 12EE(f) measures it from the date of the last entry in the profile record.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, § 12EE on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-16.
